question: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a velocity of 10 m/s . A force of 4 N is applied for 5 s . The final velocity is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: 20 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The mass of the body is given as **2 kg**, and its initial velocity is **10 m/s**.
 
• A force of **4 N** is applied to the body for a duration of **5 seconds**.
 
• The formula used to calculate the final velocity is derived from Newton's second law of motion: **v = u + (F/m) × t**, where:
 
 
• **v** is the final velocity (to be calculated).
 
• **u** is the initial velocity (10 m/s).
 
• **F** is the force applied (4 N).
 
• **m** is the mass of the body (2 kg).
 
• **t** is the time for which the force is applied (5 s).
 
 
 
• Substituting the values into the formula:
 
 
• Acceleration, **a = F/m = 4/2 = 2 m/s²**.
 
• Final velocity, v = u + a × t
